related_questions.question: What are the travel requirements to go to Hawaii?

text_blocks.snippet: For US citizens, traveling to Hawaii is considered domestic travel, so a passport is not required. A valid, government-issued photo ID like a driver's license or a REAL ID-compliant license will suffice. If you are not a US citizen, you will need a valid passport and potentially a visa, depending on your country of origin.
snippet_highlighted_words: A valid, government-issued photo ID like a driver's license or a REAL ID-compliant license will suffice

list.title: Valid Photo ID:
list.snippet: A driver's license, state-issued ID, or a REAL ID-compliant license is needed for airport security.

list.title: REAL ID Enforcement:
list.snippet: Starting May 7, 2025, the REAL ID Act will be enforced, requiring a REAL ID-compliant license or other acceptable forms of ID for domestic air travel, including to Hawaii.

list.title: No Passport Required:
list.snippet: US citizens do not need a passport for travel to Hawaii from the mainland or other US territories.
Passport: A valid passport is required for entry into the United States, including Hawaii.
Visa (Potentially): Depending on your country of origin, you may need a visa to enter the US.
ESTA: For some countries, an Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) is required.

list.title: Vaccinations:
list.snippet: While not required for entry, some vaccinations like Hepatitis A and B are recommended, especially for those visiting rural areas.

list.title: COVID-19:
list.snippet: There are no longer any COVID-related requirements for domestic travelers, including those arriving in Hawaii.

list.title: Reservations:
list.snippet: It's recommended to book flights and accommodations in advance, especially during peak travel seasons.

list.title: Respect Hawaiian Culture:
list.snippet: Familiarize yourself with local customs and traditions to ensure a respectful and enjoyable trip.
